neighbours.label: 'It' or 'If' as the first token of a new line in the middle of a text, as opposed to the same word later in a line
fire:
The storm passed over the harbor at night;
It left the boats in ruins.

How does this machine work?
It runs on steam and coal.

The minister denied the story again.
If the papers are right, he will resign.

The old bridge was closed in spring.
It reopened after the summer.

We asked her about the price.
If we pay today, it is lower.

What should you do first?
It depends on the weather.

Tickets go on sale this week.
If you hurry, you can get one.

He loved that small garden.
It reminded him of home.
quiet: The storm passed over the harbor at night; it left the boats in ruins.
How does this machine work? It runs on steam and coal.
The minister denied the story again, but if the papers are right, he will resign.
The old bridge was closed in spring, and it reopened after the summer.
We asked her about the price, and if we pay today, it is lower.
What should you do first? It depends on the weather.
Tickets go on sale this week, so if you hurry, you can get one.
He loved that small garden, and it reminded him of home.

notes: Tiny corpus max (1.41), 100% echo regime. The sentence-initial 'It' in a one-line probe reached 0.22, so 'start of a chunk' may be closer than 'new line'. In two near misses 'It' follows a question mark, a hard case.
